business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retailing of Smart IoT Devices and Home Automation

stage_1.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — federal common law with provincial civil law: Quebec limited partnerships (sociétés en commandite) are governed by the Civil Code of Québec and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2186-2251 (partnerships and limited partnerships); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-45), ss. 1, 2, 21-24, together with its General Regulation. The Canada Business Corporations Act does not apply because the registered vehicle is a Québec limited partnership, not a federal corporation. The general partner is subject to the ordinary rules of civil liability and to any express governance terms contained in the limited partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), online portal: www.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de société en commandite / Declaration of a Limited Partnership, filed electronically through the REQ's immatriculation registration service.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Québec limited partnership. Capital contributions are contractually fixed in the limited partnership agreement, credited to each limited partner's capital account when called, and need not be escrowed before registration. A nominal initial contribution is legally acceptable because creditor protection flows from public registration rather than capital maintenance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the general partner forms the Limited Partnership under the Civil Code of Québec; (2) the capital commitment subscribed by each limited partner is accepted and credited to that partner's capital account; (3) the principal establishment and registered office is set at [complete address], Province of Québec; (4) [name of representative] is appointed partnership representative, empowered to complete registration, open bank accounts, obtain tax accounts and engage professional advisors; and (5) all necessary declarations, filings and fee payments to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec are approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name validation with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online name validation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed French name and an optional English equivalent through the REQ's secure online service. REQ verifies legal availability, distinctiveness and compliance with Quebec name rules. Retain the name request reference number for use in the registration filing. The name must include 'société en commandite / limited partnership' or the recognized abbreviation 'S.E.C. / L.P.'. Confirm that the proposed name does not suggest banking, trust, insurance or other reserved activities.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name in French and optional English version
Concise business purpose description aligned with ISIC 4791
General partner name and identification details
Quebec principal establishment address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ rejects the name as unavailable or confusing, file a fresh name validation request with a different distinctive element, or request written REQ reasons and remedy the objection before proceeding. An administrative review may be requested through REQ's customer service channels.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of the limited partnership agreement and representative mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner; a Quebec notary is engaged only if immovable assets or special contributions are involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the limited partnership agreement covering management authority, capital accounts, profit and loss allocation, restrictions on limited partners, capital calls and dissolution events. Extract the technical fields required for the public declaration so the REQ filing matches the contractual terms exactly. The general partner signs the agreement and executes a notarized or authenticated power of attorney appointing the partnership representative for registration filings and banking.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement
Schedule of capital contributions and capital calls
Power of attorney appointing the REQ representative
Identification and domicile evidence for each general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the limited partnership agreement conflicts with the statutory declaration or REQ formatting rules, amend the agreement, obtain general partner consent and re-execute the power of attorney before filing the corrected declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the REQ secure filing portal and submit the Déclaration de société en commandite. Provide the validated name, Quebec principal establishment address, identification of every general partner and limited partner as requested, the limited liability statement, and contact details for the representative. Pay the statutory registration fee online and retain the transaction receipt. Do not seek bank financing or execute binding third-party contracts until the enterprise number is issued.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of a Limited Partnership
REQ name validation receipt or reference number
General partner identification and consent form
Limited partner information required by the declaration
Quebec address for service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a query or notice of deficiency, cure within 30 days of the written notice by submitting the missing information or corrected declaration through the same portal. If the registration is refused, correct the data and resubmit as a new application; any paid fee is applied to the resubmitted filing on request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the enterprise number and attestation of registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — immatriculation certificate service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the declaration is accepted, REQ issues the attestation of registration and assigns the NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec). Download the official certificate and verify the legal name, address, general partner details and limited liability indication. Store the certified PDF in the corporate records; the NEQ is the primary identifier for all subsequent filings with Revenu Québec and other Quebec government bodies.
required_dossiers: No additional document required — the attestation is generated from the accepted declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the attestation contains any data entry error, file a declaration of changes (déclaration modificative) through the REQ portal, or contact the REQ call centre to request administrative correction before using the certificate for bank or tax purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Quebec tax account registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec — clicSÉQUR Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the CRA business number has been created through REQ data exchange; if not, register online or by paper. Open a GST/HST account if taxable supplies exceed $30,000 or if early registration is elected, and register payroll deductions if employees will be hired. Register with Revenu Québec for QST, source deductions and employer contributions using the NEQ as the account identifier. Assign the general partner as the authorized contact for all tax authorities.
required_dossiers: REQ attestation of registration and NEQ
General partner identification
Bank details for CRA and Revenu Québec refunds
Payroll data and estimated remuneration, if applicable
GST/HST account application and effective date
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec accounts are not automatically linked to the NEQ, submit paper forms RC1 (CRA) and LM-1-V (Revenu Québec) with a copy of the REQ attestation, and escalate by telephone to the CRA business line at 1-800-959-5525 or Revenu Québec at 1-800-567-4692.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and capital contribution call
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I Canadian bank or Quebec credit union, e.g. RBC, BMO, Desjardins
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the REQ attestation, limited partnership agreement, initial general partner resolution and all authorized signing officer identification to the financial institution. Open the account in the name of the limited partnership, not in the name of the general partner personally. Deposit the agreed initial capital contributions only when called under the partnership agreement and preserve deposit slips and account statements as evidence of each capital account. Ensure all signing officers are named in the partnership records.
required_dossiers: REQ attestation of registration
Limited partnership agreement
Initial general partner resolution
Government-issued identification for each signing officer
Beneficial ownership information required by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests supplementary proof of authority or a local service address, obtain a secretary's certificate or updated REQ extract and resubmit. If the bank delays, select another Schedule I institution; Quebec credit unions commonly accept REQ attestation as sufficient formation evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-opening workplace, fire safety and municipal licence check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal permit office of the relevant Quebec city or arrondissement; local fire prevention service; CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify local zoning and determine whether a municipal business permit (permis d'affaires) is required for the planned retail storefront. Request a fire safety inspection where the premises are open to the public. If employees will be hired, register with CNESST as an employer and comply with the Act respecting occupational health and safety. Maintain proof of premises control and inspection certificates in the partnership records before the first day of operation.
required_dossiers: Lease or proof of right of occupation
Municipal business licence application, if applicable
Fire safety inspection request and clearance
CNESST employer registration, if applicable
Retail signage permits, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal permit is refused, revise the application to comply with zoning or fire codes and appeal through the municipal administrative process. If fire clearance is withheld, correct the flagged deficiencies, such as exiting, extinguishers or occupancy load, and request a re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — retail and warehousing of smart-home IoT hardware under ISIC 4791 is not a regulated industrial activity in Quebec; no provincial industrial licensing board must approve the operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial operating or manufacturing licence is required. A municipal business permit and fire safety clearance may apply if a physical retail location is opened; such permits are municipal in nature rather than provincial industry licences.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the retail sale of consumer IoT hardware does not constitute a class of activity listed for environmental impact assessment under the Environmental Quality Act (CQLR c E-12.1). An EIA registration or full report would be triggered only if the partnership later operates an industrial facility, waste treatment site or other scheduled activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated industrial wastewater or VOC emission source is present in a retail IoT hardware operation. Electronic and battery waste from returned products must be managed under Quebec's extended producer responsibility regimes administered with Recyc-Québec; general waste must be removed in accordance with municipal waste bylaws and the residual contamination standards of the Environmental Quality Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The retail place of business must comply with the Québec Building Code and Québec Fire Safety Code; a fire safety inspection is required before public occupancy where local regulation mandates it. Employer workplaces must comply with the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1), including CNESST registration, training and reporting obligations if staff are hired. Structural load inspections are not applicable to ordinary retail fit-outs unless the building is modified.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agence du revenu du Québec (Revenu Québec) - Portal: Revenu Québec Online Services (clients.revenuquebec.ca); Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Portal: My Business Account (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign limited partnership carrying on business in Quebec must: (1) register with the CRA for a federal Business Number (BN) via Business Registration Online or Form RC1; (2) open a GST/HST account (program account RT) and, if importing goods, an import/export account (RM); (3) register separately with Revenu Québec for the QST using the BN, via Revenu Québec Online Services or Form LM-1-V; (4) for non-resident partnerships, registration is mandatory when the partnership makes taxable supplies in Canada or solicits orders in Canada, subject to the small supplier threshold; (5) each registration must be completed before the obligation to collect tax arises, typically before the first sale to a Quebec consumer or before goods are imported into Canada; the QST registration number is displayed on all invoices as 'QST registration number'.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A limited partnership is fiscally transparent for Canadian and Quebec income tax purposes: no tax is payable at the partnership level; income or loss is allocated to partners in accordance with the limited partnership agreement. There is no 'check-the-box' election for Canadian LPs; however, partners may elect under section 96(3) of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and section 681.1 of the Taxation Act (Quebec) to compute income at partnership level differently for certain inter-provincial rules. Hybrid mismatch elections are available under sections 18.2 and 18.3 of the Income Tax Act and corresponding Quebec rules, addressing mismatched payments between Canada and foreign jurisdictions where an LP is treated as opaque abroad.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (excluding financial services) in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters. QST: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies (excluding financial services) in Quebec or Canada in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; non-resident persons are also required to register if they solicit orders in Canada or enter Canada to perform services, regardless of threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Quebec mandates electronic invoicing and real-time reporting for B2B transactions through the Revenu Québec 'facturation électronique' system (based on the PEPPOL network). Registered suppliers must transmit invoice data to Revenu Québec in near real time (no later than the time of issue for larger taxpayers; phased implementation for smaller suppliers). The invoice must include QST registration number, BN, date, supplier/customer names, total amount, and QST/GST breakdown. There is no federal real-time clearance mandate for GST/HST; however, all electronic records must be retained and made available to the CRA on request. For export goods, an electronic export declaration must be filed with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CAERS) before goods exit Canada.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (i) supplies of goods exported by the supplier (Part V, Schedule VI, Excise Tax Act); (ii) supplies of services performed in respect of exported goods; (iii) supplies of services to a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST and where the service is not for use in Canada; and (iv) certain supplies of goods delivered by the supplier to a common carrier for export. For QST, analogous zero-rating rules apply under Schedule III to the QST Act. Conditions: goods must be exported 'as soon as is reasonable' and documentary proof of export must be retained; if goods are not exported within 60 days of delivery, zero-rating is denied unless the delay is due to exigent circumstances. A registrant that zero-rates must maintain evidence of export in its books and records for six years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A / A1/A6 or electronic CAERS declaration)
Bill of Lading (ocean, air, or truck waybill)
Commercial invoice showing the vendor's and purchaser's names and addresses, description, and value
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank wire or payment receipt evidencing receipt of payment in foreign currency from the foreign buyer)
Proof of delivery to the foreign destination (signed delivery receipt or customs entry at destination)
Carrier certificate of export (if relied upon to show export within 60 days)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Québec regularly audit exporters' zero-rating claims. If an export is not substantiated with the required documentation, the tax authority may reassess the supply as taxable, and the supplier becomes liable for the uncollected GST/QST (currently 14.975% in Quebec), plus interest and penalties. Penalties include: GST/HST false statement penalties under section 285 of the Excise Tax Act (up to 50% of the amount at issue), Revenu Québec penalties under section 1083 of the Taxation Act (Quebec) (up to 50%), and gross negligence penalties under the Income Tax Act where applicable. In aggravated cases, criminal prosecution may be pursued, with fines up to CAD 100,000 and imprisonment up to five years for tax evasion. Retrospective clawbacks are generally limited to the standard statutory reassessment period (four years for GST/HST and QST), which is extended to seven years or unlimited in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or neglect.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); with foreign exchange supervision administered by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and anti-money-laundering oversight by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). The Minister of Finance retains residual policy authority over exchange matters under the Currency Act and the Financial Administration Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains liberalized current and capital account convertibility under the IMF Articles of Agreement. No exchange control approvals are required for inward or outward remittances, profit repatriation, or partnership distributions. Non-resident partners of a Quebec limited partnership may freely remit earnings in CAD or other convertible currencies, subject only to Part XIII withholding taxes of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and applicable treaty relief. Banks independently perform source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership due diligence before effecting transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory export proceeds surrender rules operate in Canada. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation, no minimum conversion ratio, and no obligation to force-convert export receipts into CAD. Exporters may retain foreign currency balances and convert at negotiated commercial rates. Cross-border movements of CAD 10,000 or more require reporting to FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Non-resident electronic money institutions may clear CAD payments only if they have registered as a money service business (MSB) with FINTRAC, maintain a Canadian legal agent, and implement a compliant AML/ATF program. Pure offshore EMIs without Canadian registration cannot open direct clearing accounts or operate as payment intermediaries for a Quebec LP. The practical clear path is to use Canadian licensed payment processors such as Stripe or Shopify Payments for retail transactions and restrict offshore EMIs to settlement convenience products.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors or general partner representatives are not statutorily required to appear physically at the bank's branch. Enhanced remote video KYC is generally accepted by tier-1 Canadian banks, provided the individuals verify identity through a notarized or bank-guaranteed digital identity process. A Quebec limited partnership must maintain a registered office and registered agent in Quebec; the general partner or its authorized representative must deliver certified organizational documents, identification, and authority resolutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Obscure beneficial ownership structure through a chain of limited partners, especially with non-resident partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed beneficial ownership schedule; certified copy of the declaration of partnership; register of partners with percentages; general partner's certified certificate and corporate records; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations; Canadian Business Number (BN/NE) registration evidence; notarized identification for all signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geographic source of inbound capital related to investor remittances
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank references from originator financial institutions; confirmed SWIFT MT103 messages; investor bank statements covering at least 6 months; source of wealth letter; constitutional documents of the capital provider; evidence of the underlying commercial or investment agreement; AML/CFT questionnaire response.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between declared retail activity and third-party supplier payments for IoT hardware
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices matching purchase orders; bill of lading and airway bills; INCOTERMS contracts; logistics tracking records; supplier KYC pack; product catalog and customs classification (HS codes under 8517 or 8471 where applicable); explanation of payment chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Accidental MSB classification due to high-volume digital payment collection and payouts to merchants or partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC MSB registration confirmation or a legal opinion confirming exemption; written AML/ATF policy and risk assessment; appointed compliance officer; transactional records demonstrating the LP is selling its own inventory and does not operate a payment intermediary service; explanation of the retail business model.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or capital contributions from foreign partners are routed through SWIFT MT103 (or domestic large-value wire via the Canadian Payments Association's Large Value Transfer System, LVTS) with the payment purpose coded as 'EQUITY INJECTION' or 'CAPITAL INVESTMENT'. The Quebec LP must provide a board/partner resolution approving the injection, the concession or partnership agreement, the source-of-funds declaration, and the Canadian Business Number. No exchange control permit is required; the receiving bank verifies the sender and the transaction narrative, and may require confirmation that the funds are not derived from proceeds of crime.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments to foreign IoT hardware manufacturers are cleared through SWIFT MT103 for direct bank-to-bank USD/EUR/CNY transfers, or through Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) for high-value procurement. Domestic CAD payments are cleared via the CPA Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) or LVTS for same-day settlement. A tier-1 Canadian bank trade desk will validate invoices, shipping documents, and Incoterms before releasing funds under the trade finance framework.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards against CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/CNY
FX swaps for short-term liquidity rebalancing
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for matched funding of long-term partner loans
Vanilla FX options to hedge uncertain trade settlement volumes
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or less-liquid emerging-market currencies accompanying trade corridors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary month of the initial REQ registration; declaration period opens 30 days before the anniversary date and closes on that date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty of CAD 250 (approx. USD 190) for late filing; persistent non-filing results in a REQ notice and potential administrative striking-off from the Quebec enterprise register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership fiscal year-end (for a December 31 year-end, on or before May 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per partner per month, up to CAD 300 per partner (12-month maximum); continued default may trigger judicial reassessment of partnership allocations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: TP-600 Partnership Income Tax Return (Revenu Québec) and RL-15 partner slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the partnership fiscal year-end (for a December 31 year-end, on or before June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger Revenu Québec penalties and interest and may suspend recognition of partnership allocations until the return is accepted

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No Quebec statutory audit threshold for a private limited partnership; an independent audit is mandatory only if required by the partnership agreement, a lender or statutory covenant, or securities legislation governing public-market participation
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian ASPE Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook as the default private-enterprise framework; IFRS is required if the LP is a publicly accountable enterprise

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual REQ declaration re-confirms all partners, the general partner identification, and the registered office/address service; any transfer, redemption, or contribution change affecting partner identity or liability status must be recorded in the LP minute book and reflected in the next annual declaration, with early REQ amendment where registered particulars change
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (identifying general and limited partners and their contributions)
Limited Partner Contributions and Withdrawals Ledger
Minute Book of General Partner Meetings and Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – 450 per year (CAD 200 – 600) for a registered office agent and annual declaration processing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 20,000 per year for a certified audit, if contractually or lender-required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the Limited Partnership (LP) entity level because the LP is fiscally transparent; combined federal+Quebec general corporate income tax rate for a corporate partner is 26.5% (15% federal Part I + 11.5% Quebec provincial)
